The most famous example of Carti referencing Cudi is a leaked song, ‘Pissy Pamper’ or more recognisably, ‘Kid Cudi’. He raps:

Brand new pack like Kid Cudi,

Though the song was never released, the song quickly topped the Spotify US Viral 50 chart before being removed. The song would repeatedly be uploaded under different names, constantly charting before being removed.

meaning:
Playboi Carti refers to the idea that individuals with private access to exclusive parties or events can enter through the backdoor rather than the front.

The phrase “Members Only” is also closely associated with the American hip-hop collective Members Only, founded in 2014 by XXXTentacion and Ski Mask the Slump God.

On August 25, 2017, Kendrick Lamar tweeted and shared XXXTentacion’s album 17. A month earlier, on July 12, 2017, XXXTentacion opened for Kendrick Lamar during the North American leg of The DAMN. Tour.

That same day, Playboi Carti and XXXTentacion were featured in XXL’s 2017 Freshman Class.

When Kendrick Lamar references “Members only, rising through the backdoor,” he is paying homage to XXXTentacion and recognizing both him and Playboi Carti as “members.”

Many have conspired that Drake was involved in XXXTENTACION’s murder. This could potentially be Kendrick calling Drake out/dissing him

Drake also has a song called “Members Only”.

“Backdoor” could symbolize underhanded tactics, hinting at the long-standing accusations that Drake uses ghostwriters instead of writing his own lyrics. Kendrick might be suggesting that Drake gets ahead in the industry through non-traditional means rather than raw talent.

The phrase “backdoor” could be a double entendre referring to rumors about Drake’s relationships, implying that he sneaks around or lacks the confidence to be upfront in personal matters.

By using “Members Only” in his line, Kendrick could be mocking Drake’s attempt to claim exclusivity or authenticity. He might be implying that Drake isn’t actually a real “member” of the culture, but rather someone who forces his way in or takes shortcuts (riding through the backdoor).

line: My grandma still play bingo
vault_lines: I was in the spot yesterday with my pops, my grandma still play bingo
meaning:
This line serves as a social commentary on consumerism’s waning impact amongst the lives of the elderly and highlights the importance of prioritising immaterial experiences in an avaricious, money-centric society.

In a somewhat unexpected deviation from the bourgeois ideology usually perpetuated in his lyrics, Carti draws attention to his grandmother’s lifestyle, which is seemingly unaffected by the benefit of Carti’s acquired riches. With or without excessive financial security, his grandmother’s daily routine is unchanged, emphasising the irrelevance of affluence in one’s senior years.

Ironically, unlike the game of ‘Bingo’, financial freedom does not provide the tools needed to ‘tick all of life’s boxes’; with happinesses and health on no account the byproduct of wealth.

In addition, this lyric in particular accentuates the perceived immediacy of Carti’s ascent to stardom. Although his near-decade spanning career may not be the epitome of so-called ‘overnight success’, for someone as senior as a grandmother, ten years is a proportionately short period of time.

meaning:
By using the number 23, Carti refers to two things; the first and most obvious is the number worn by renowned Ohio native basketball player LeBron James, and the second is the Glock 23, a type of .40 caliber semi-automatic pistol.

“Heat” is a slang term for a gun or a stash of guns. By mentioning the word, Carti is also referencing to the time James spent on the Miami Heat NBA team from 2011 to 2014.

Carti not only makes a simple comparison between the model of his pistol and LeBron’s number—by mentioning how he drives through the streets of Miami drugged in a car from the luxury brand Rolls-Royce, he is also making an implicit reference to the fact that, although neither of them is originally from there, both frequent Miami thanks to the success that their work brought.

The lines could be, in addition to a creative analogy, a shout-out to LeBron himself, who in 2017, through a video shared by DJ Steph Floss, was seen dancing along Kyrie Irving to “Magnolia” during a Cleveland Cavaliers training.

This is not the first time Playboi has referenced a pistol from the manufacturer Glock in his songs, he has already done so in songs like “wokeuplikethis*,” “Half & Half,” or “Poke It Out.” He has also been caught holding a Glock 17.

In religious context, the St. Peters cross, is not just a religious cross, but it’s also an anti-religious cross, with reason being Because Peter was the rock upon which the church of Jesus Christ was built upon, this symbol of the upside down cross was highly significant, and became a part of Christian iconography. It symbolized the papacy, because the Pope is considered Peter’s successor and the Bishop of Rome. It was used in churches and in Christian artwork to symbolize humility and unworthiness when compared to Jesus. In Catholicism, the inverted cross is accepted and valued, but an inverted crucifix is not. To clarify, a crucifix features an image of Jesus on the cross. If a crucifix is inverted, it appears as disrespectful and irreverent. Likewise, the Petrine cross became associated with anti-Christian perceptions and the satanic church. This is simply because, as a visual symbol, it’s the opposite of the Latin cross and so can be viewed as having opposite connotations. As the cross is the most recognized symbol of Christianity, an upside down cross could represent anti-Christian sentiments. This is the same with the pentagram, which has Christian symbolism but when inverted, is believed to represent evil and to attract dark forces. This view has been greatly promoted by popular culture and media, where the upside down cross is portrayed as something evil and satanic.

line: I promised Playboi we’d get the tape out ’fore the weekend is over
vault_lines: I promised Playboi we'd get the tape out 'fore the weekend is over
meaning:
After more than two years since Whole Lotta Red was initially announced by Playboi Carti, fans were finally starting to see the light at the end of the tunnel towards the end of 2020. After countless missed deadlines, many signs led fans to believe the album would release before the end of the year. This all culminated on November 23, with Carti dropping a bombshell onto his Instagram: according to himself, the album was turned in.

However, given that a clip of DJ Akademiks from December 10 appears on “Control,” it’s clear that the album had been worked on after the supposed turn-in date. During the time between then and December 25, the album was being worked on at Kanye West’s infamous Wyoming property, with Kanye executive producing the project. Many fans speculate that much of the album was re-recorded during this time, which would explain why some people think the album sounds “rushed.”

Kanye himself is no stranger to making last-minute changes to his albums, sometimes completely reworking them, usually leading to release dates being missed–almost every album of his career has been delayed past a promised release date. An exception to this would be Kanye’s June 2018 project Ye. The album’s release date of June 1 was announced on April 19 and actually released on the promised date. However, since April, the album had been entirely reworked, barely managing to meet this deadline. According to collaborator 070 Shake, the track “Ghost Town” was finished “the same day it came out.”

Much like the rest of this verse, this line was repurposed from Kanye’s verse from the demo of Future’s 2016 song “In Abundance,” on which he rapped:

I promised Future we’d get the tape out ‘fore the weekend is over

Here, Ye replaces “wolf” with “wolverine,” a ferocious animal and mutant superhero character from the Marvel universe, suggesting that his tendencies to hide his true intentions are more severe than for most. As a result, this could be an allusion to Bipolar disorder, a condition with which Ye has previously been diagnosed.

Kanye tackled a similar theme on his 2016 song, “Wolves,” in which he discussed his frailty and his fear for the danger of his own family’s purity:

vault_lines: I'm so addicted to drugs (I'm so addicted to drugs)
meaning:
Carti’s repetition of this very personal exposition of substance use might seem to some listeners as filler and or nonsense, but Carti is infamously known to use bar repetition to highlight themes, and this continuous “hammering in” of the line stresses the importance of a subject that usually is recruited into the general theme of Carti’s lyricism to help guarantee his iconic “exposé de glamour,” aesthetic, a hyper-materialistic circus of elegant linguistic tricks involving high-end fashion, designer substances, chemicals, pills, liquids, women, money, and what it brings, good or bad.

Carti encapsulates his personification of late-stage capitalism and its effects on minority perceptions of individual-level success to ensure achievement of a specific brand of “cool” akin to vintage playboy advertisements. A certain chic mystery mojo man, that has persisted since the Italian new wave, but insisted ever longer.  The upheaval of such a vintage tone and trope involves the dramatization of all forms of vice, including simulated freedom, most times, and to stimulate differentiation, the lack thereof.

Carti shows two manic differences in the admittance of his substance abuse and more importantly, his addiction’s negative role, manically switching from one to the other, rather than allowing to be shown attempting any natural daunting human restraint in lifestyle.

Carti lives and breathes 20th century Playboy after-party Hefner jacuzzi vibes, as well as 4 AM naked stimulant crash breakdown vibes. Yet he always keeps them guessing, and even in his most honestly human bars, leave us with a tone full of passions, waiting to be perceived by others to be aligned with their own vindications.

Being an unreleased song, Carti might have sought to not publicly release a song with such a harrowing depiction of a topic usually seen as positive throughout Die Lit and other projects which see official release.

This concept of a bird’s-eye view can also be seen as a metaphor for gaining a higher perspective or understanding, similar to how some artists, like Kanye West during his Yandhi-era, have used the “bird’s-eye view” approach to illustrate their grasp on life, the law of attraction, and the notion that reality itself is a kind of game—one where individuals can “run the streets” and command influence using their voice and vision:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ahOIJNLLtkI

Additionally, British rapper Skepta joined the world of GTA V as the co-host of iFruit Radio, adding to the game’s cultural immersion with his music and commentary.

Amassing fame and fortune from posting music on SoundCloud during the peak of the website’s stratospheric careers trajectories made accessible to many “SoundCloud rappers”, arguably from 2015 to 2019, Playboi Carti’s professional career is subject to intense volatility.

Carti is stressing the importance of maintaining a successful career as an artist by keeping his music away from subjection to hype: attention which is gained easily and lost quickly. Carti’s revolutionary strides in his music curation ensures he does not face the threat of “falling off” as many of his peers have suffered.

Many rappers who lift similar styles used and curated in Carti’s mixtapes often rely on internet hype accrued from profligate displays of wealth. This model of sustaining fame rarely leaves their career anywhere else but the unknown; kids on the internet grow up, the hype dies. However, Carti successfully subverts this pitfall through disruptive music curation: he constantly defies his artistry, letting go of any presumptions or marketing stunts which would compromise the creative risks evidently abundant in his 2020 album Whole Lotta Red.

meaning:
“‘Bout that shit” is a phrase commonly used in hip-hop when discussing someone’s authenticity in the way they present themselves. Rappers commonly call out their adversaries for fronting falsified lifestyles with this phrase, whether it be an elevated sense of violence, gang activity, drug use or selling, or any number of illicit activities that may be associated with a “hard” lifestyle.

For example, on Young Nudy and Pi'erre Bourne’s unreleased track “Pissy Pamper” with Carti, Nudy claims that everything he and Carti show to the public is authentic:

We don’t talk that shit (Nah)
We be ‘bout that shit (We be 'bout that shit)
We gotta walk it, we gotta talk it
Nigga, be about it (Nigga, be about it)

Carti also addressed the fact that he has never felt the need to front in his career in a March 2017 interview with FADER:

Ever since I was a little kid, my mama will tell you, I always been the type to just show, instead of tellin' you about it.

After being pulled over for an expired tag, police discovered marijuana and firearms in his car. In the lines “I got niggas in chain gang on my side / I had the niggas shank Ola for a pie”, Carti claims to have had his friends in jail stab and rob Ola for a mere pie.

In prison, pies and other food are a highly valued commodity that are oftentimes bartered as a currency. Alternatively, Carti could be referring to a kilogram of cocaine, which pie is also a slang term for.

Carti also says “Smokin' on the Henchmen”, which is a diss aimed at Ola’s Henchmen gang.

Front Street is an area of Atlanta frequented by the Henchmen. Ola’s close friend Woo da Savage took to Instagram to respond to the diss, claiming Carti had never even been to Front Street.

The former, an amphetamine, and the latter, an opioid, have counteractive effects, with ecstasy acting as a stimulant and codeine acting as a depressant. However, dosing both “uppers” and “downers” at the same time does not cancel out the effects of both – the combination can lead to fatal effects such as dehydration, overheating, and the production of toxic byproducts within the body.

Both artists have utilized their drug use as a trope within their music. In fact, both Carti and Future have songs titled after both of the aforementioned drugs:




 
 Codeine 
 MDMA 




 Carti 
 “Lean 4 Real”  
 “No Stylist / Molly”  


 Hndrx 
 “Codeine Crazy”  
 “Double Cups & Molly” 





Both artists also have documented histories with the drugs. On April 2, 2020, Carti was pulled over for expired tags on his car. Law enforcement officers who pulled over Carti ended up finding codeine within the vehicle after a search was carried out. While never having been caught with the drug, Future spoke on how his rap career put the drug into the spotlight for many young people, including the late rapper Juice WRLD, in a January 2019 interview with Rolling Stone:

I made it seem so cool, I made it seem so fucking cool[…] When he told me that, I was like ‘Oh shit. What the fuck have I done? It really bothered me. It bothered me a lot. More than that I thought it would bother me when he told me that. I didn’t think I’d care about that stuff. Four years ago, I probably wouldn’t have cared if he told me: ‘Oh, that was good you was drinking.’ Now it’s like, ‘Oh shit.’ How many other sixth-graders did I influence to drink lean?

line: I’m on the X, I’m on the codeine (Yeah, yeah) I’m on the X, I’m on the codeine (Yeah, yeah) I’m on the X, I’m on the codeine (Woo, yeah) I’m on the X, I’m on the codeine (Hold up, talkin’ ’bout) We on the X, we on the codeine (Yeah, talkin’ ’bout) We on the X, we on the codeine (Yeah, yeah, yeah) We on the X, we on the codeine (Woo, woo, woo) We on the X, we on the codeine
vault_lines: We on the X, we on the codeine
meaning:
Ecstasy, a street name for MDMA and abbreviated by “X,” and codeine are two designer drugs that both Carti and Future have frequently mentioned in their music throughout both of their careers.

The former, an amphetamine, and the latter, an opioid, have counteractive effects, with ecstasy acting as a stimulant and codeine acting as a depressant. However, dosing both “uppers” and “downers” at the same time does not cancel out the effects of both – the combination can lead to fatal effects such as dehydration, overheating, and the production of toxic byproducts within the body.

Both artists have utilized their drug use as a trope within their music.

Both artists also have documented histories with the drugs. On April 2, 2020, Carti was pulled over for expired tags on his car. Law enforcement officers who pulled over Carti ended up finding codeine within the vehicle after a search was carried out. While never having been caught with the drug, Future spoke on how his rap career put the drug into the spotlight for many young people, including the late rapper Juice WRLD, in a January 2019 interview with Rolling Stone:

I made it seem so cool, I made it seem so fucking cool[…] When he told me that, I was like ‘Oh shit. What the fuck have I done? It really bothered me. It bothered me a lot. More than that I thought it would bother me when he told me that. I didn’t think I’d care about that stuff. Four years ago, I probably wouldn’t have cared if he told me: ‘Oh, that was good you was drinking.’ Now it’s like, ‘Oh shit.’ How many other sixth-graders did I influence to drink lean?

meaning:
Throughout the track Carti explains that he is not one to ‘talk about’ doing ‘that shit’ in which ‘that shit’ involves a number of high-adrenaline and potentially dangerous activities such as selling drugs, engaging in violent shootouts, and having affairs with the spouses of others, but instead actually participates in these activities.

This line stands out from the rest since ‘that shit’ which Carti performs instead of talking about is not the usual high-impact antics which are spread throughout the rest of the track. Instead, that thing that Carti is doing instead of talking about is something that you and I might be well familiar with; shooting the shit. ‘Shoot the shit’ is an English phrase which is derived from another, ‘shoot the breeze.’ Both phrases mean to have a casual conversation or to participate in small talk. Thus, while Carti considers making money from the drug trade and participating in violence with firearms to be important activities which he does while others only talk about doing them, Carti also elevates small talk to the same level of importance as those activities with this line.

This has a twofold effect. First, Carti recognizes that small interactions with others are equally as important to the good life as these other, potentially life-threatening, activities. This sentiment is perhaps a commentary on the absurdist philosophy of Albert Camus. In the first sentence of perhaps his most famous work, The Myth of Sisyphus Camus posits the following: “There is but one truly serious philosophical problem, and that is suicide” and has been quoted demanding that men contemplate if one should kill oneself or have a cup of coffee. Indeed, the notion that shooting the shit could be, for Carti, something which warrants the same level of contemplation (and importantly for Carti, action) as those other highly dangerous activities is a way in which Carti, like Camus, attempts to describe the absurdity of the modern life: One cannot live with small talk, life is much grander that that, but one must nonetheless participate in small talk if they want to go about truly living.

Second, it should be remembered that Carti is listing activities which others only talk about doing while failing to actually do them. Carti, on the other hand, really does participate in these activities. The listener is forced to reconcile within himself the extent to which he himself takes for granted these small interactions of shooting the shit without truly participating in them. While others simply talk to one another (and, for Carti, talk about talking to one another) they fail to examine the importance of these interactions. When on trial for his life in Athens, Socrates, the teacher of the founder of the Western philosophical tradition, Plato, said that “the unexamined life is not worth living.” These words are echoed here in Carti who suggests that it is he, and not others, who examines these small interactions of shooting the shit and is therefore able to claim that he is actually participating in them. Others do not examine, they do not live, they therefore do not do that shit.
